From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Ben / Grace — attaching MSA_v3_redlines.docx (redline). Quick flags from Legal after an initial pass:

1) Term / auto-renew: Acme is likely to push for an 18-month maximum and a shorter auto-renew notice window. Recommend we propose a mutual 12-18 month option; keep auto-renew but add explicit notice and an auto-terminate if pricing materially changes.

2) Indemnity / cap: Proposed change to carve out certain IP indemnities. We should preserve Redwood's standard cap but offer a limited carve for third-party IP in narrow circumstances.

3) Data residency / audit: Procurement asked about SOC 2 artifacts — we can provide SOC 2 Type II plus a summary of KMS integrations. However, Acme is asking for a quarterly access log export; recommend offering quarterly attestation instead of raw log exports.

4) SLA credits: Their draft requested cumulative credits > 20% for multi-incident months. We'll offer clarified SLOs and a per-incident credit formula capped at 15% monthly.

5) Order form clarity: I added a coverage ledger table in the order form to map token/throughput tiers to billing lines; this should address procurement's unit-econ questions.

Please review the redlines and advise which of these points are commercial deal-breakers for the AM. If you want, I can join procurement's call to walk through the clauses.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

-----
Attachment: MSA_v3_redlines.docx (tracked changes; key clauses commented)

From: Claire Park <claire.park@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal request + 30% capacity bump — docs for procurement

Thanks Ben and Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround and the coverage ledger idea. A few procurement constraints up-front so legal can factor them into negotiation:

- Max term: 18 months hard cap. No auto-renew longer than 30 days notice.
- Audit logs: procurement prefers a monthly export to a secure SFTP. Security prefers attestation instead, but procurement wants the export as fallback.
- SLA credits: procurement will not accept a single-incident cap that prevents escalation across consecutive incidents. They want cumulative relief for multi-day incidents.

I've attached our constraints spreadsheet (Acme_Procurement_Constraints.xlsx) with the sections they'll redline. Happy to do a joint call Thu 10am PT — I've tentatively booked that slot.

Claire
